hook: A fleshy lump that fell from orbit with an ordinary apartment inside it is a strange, vivid premise. The article is short and reads quickly. Pay attention to the furniture list, because it does most of the storytelling.
whyItMatters: With one of the lowest numbers on the site, it is among the first files many readers open. It shows how much a compact, eerie premise can carry without long documentation, and its body horror works almost entirely through a dry inventory rather than on-page scenes.
thingsToNotice:
The furniture is made of people. The lamps, rug, beanbag chair, children's toys and potted plant turn out to be carved bone, woven hair and other human tissue, each piece carrying its own DNA, and the count of seven missing staff sits right beside the list so the reader does the math. Animals and corpses do nothing to it; only living humans get turned into decor.

The discovery report adds a second horror: three villagers sent inside vanish, four guards are pulled in during transport, and General Mulhausen responds by ordering every witness killed, roughly a third of the village. Two expunged blocks follow, and the next thing we learn is that Mulhausen himself was terminated, which explains why command staff must now give up their rank and go in under heavy escort. The window with no outside opening and the rule about keeping a hand on your partner hint that the room also works on the mind of whoever stands near it.
